title: A skew conference matrix of order 20 whose row code over F_19 is not MDS: a counterexample to Conjecture 5 of Etzion, Vardy and Yaakobi (arXiv:1210.5725; IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 59 (2013) Conjecture 1)
exact_endpoint: ConferenceMDS.conjecture5_false : ¬ ConferenceMDS.Conjecture5, where Conjecture5 := ∀ p, p.Prime → ∀ W : Matrix (Fin (p+1)) (Fin (p+1)) ℤ, IsConferenceMatrix W → IsMDS (rowCode p W) ∧ finrank (rowCode p W) = (p+1)/2 ∧ minDistance (rowCode p W) = (p+3)/2, with the source's weighing-matrix definition of conference matrix and the F_p row span (proved equal to the source's lattice reduction for all p, n, W)
scope: Etzion-Vardy-Yaakobi conjecture that the code of length p + 1 over Z_p generated by a conference matrix of order p + 1 is MDS of dimension (p+1)/2 and minimum distance (p+3)/2. False at p = 19: an explicit Goethals-Seidel skew conference matrix of order 20 has an F_19 row code of dimension 10 containing a nonzero codeword of weight 9 < 11.
source_targets: Etzion-Vardy-Yaakobi arXiv:1210.5725 Conjecture 5 / IEEE TIT 2013 Conjecture 1

substantive_reason: It refutes a conjecture stated in a peer-reviewed IEEE Transactions paper and listed there as open problem 2, which the authors had verified only for Paley matrices (whose row codes are Reed-Solomon codes). The explicit non-Paley skew conference matrix shows the universal MDS claim fails. Significance is a qualified pass at the minimum threshold: a single finite counterexample found by search, with no infinite family.
